François Judith Paul Grévy (15 August 1807 – 9 September 1891), known as Jules Grévy ( French: [ʒyl ɡʁevi] ), was a French lawyer and politician who served as President of France from 1879 to 1887. He was a leader of the Moderate Republicans , and given that his predecessors were monarchists who tried without success to restore the French monarchy, Grévy is considered the first real republican president of France. [ 2 ] [ 3 ] During Grévy's presidency from 1879 to 1887, according to David Bell, there was a disunity among his cabinets. Only one survived  more than a year. Grévy paid attention chiefly to defense, internal order, and foreign relations. Critics argue that Grévy's confusing approach to appointments set a bad precedent for handling crises.
